summary: Move a finite supplied occupant count through a directed route network with integer travel steps, per-step arc capacities and a declared blocked-edge event, as an educational capacity scenario rather than an evacuation-safety result.
objective: Move a finite supplied occupant count through a directed route network with integer travel steps, per-step arc capacities and a declared blocked-edge event, as an educational capacity scenario rather than an evacuation-safety result.
example_prompts: Build finite egress-network capacity playback with explicit stable IDs, units, time, boundary inputs and stale/unavailable states.
not_for: Safety certification, regulatory compliance, or operational control without qualified local review.

entities.name: Route graph
entities.guidance: Store stable space/portal/exit IDs, directed connectivity, integer travel steps and supplied persons-per-step capacities; geometry proximity never creates an edge.

entities.name: Occupant queues
entities.guidance: Initialize integer counts at source nodes and preserve every queued, in-transit and exited person in the ledger.

entities.name: Blocked-edge event
entities.guidance: At one declared step set selected arc capacity to zero for future dispatch; occupants already in transit retain their scheduled arrival.

state_contract.model: Accept 1..64 nodes, 1..128 directed arcs, 1..10000 integer occupants and finite horizon H<=10000. Each arc has integer travel delay>=1 and integer dispatch capacity>=0 persons/step. At initialization, move every occupant placed at an exit directly to exited count; reject an exit placement if this convention is not desired. At step k, deliver previously scheduled arrivals, then visit nodes/arcs in stable ID order and dispatch up to residual arc capacity according to a supplied deterministic next-arc priority; schedule arrival at k+delay. Exit nodes absorb arrivals. A declared block changes future capacity only. Stop at H, all-exited, or invalid route; do not infer capacity from doorway mesh width.
state_contract.authority: The supplied graph/capacities/routing/event ledger owns counts. Blender authors spaces, portals and route anchors with stable IDs; glTF carries static geometry/IDs; Three.js owns queues, scheduled arrivals, conservation, block state and reset.
actions: Inspect one node/arc queue and throughput.

invariants: initial occupants = queued + in-transit + exited at every accepted step.
Initial exit-node occupants are absorbed into exited count before step zero, never left queued.
Dispatch never exceeds declared arc capacity.
Blocked capacity affects no already-dispatched occupant.
No-clearance or safety verdict is derived from completion time.
motion_guidance: Playback restores stored model/event steps; animation between steps is explanatory and never changes authoritative counts, timestamps or completion state.
creative_affordances: Use cutaways, small multiples, queues and non-color status glyphs while keeping assumptions and unavailable states visible.
known_limits: Capacities, routes and initial counts are supplied scenario inputs, not code-derived compliance values. No crowd interaction, smoke, human behavior, local-code review or runtime execution.

claims.statement: NIST IR 7425 studies building evacuation with differential egress capacity when emergency responders use stairs, demonstrating that egress-capacity assumptions and counterflow scenarios materially belong in an explicitly declared model.
claims.scope: NIST 2007 report context only; this recipe’s discrete graph, routing order, capacities and block event are authored educational rules and are not code compliance.

source_refs.locator: Linked official IR PDF, Abstract and Modeling Scenario sections

object_craft.structure: Blender separates floors, stairs, portals and exits into named static parts and places stable route anchors; glTF exports geometry/IDs, never occupant counts or inferred connectivity.
object_craft.material: Open, queued, blocked and exit states use glyph plus pattern; corridor width is not a capacity legend.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js builds arcs only from supplied IDs, instantiates count glyphs, updates queues/in-transit schedules and exact reset.

physical_contract.scope: Finite deterministic capacitated network scenario; no collision, crowd behavior or safety model.
physical_contract.timestep: One declared model step with arrivals delivered before stable-order dispatch.
checks: Blocked-edge fixture preserves prior in-transit arrivals.
